alerts.title: AKI on TDF: consider temporary hold, not permanent stop
alerts.message: Guidelines list acute kidney injury as a TDF toxicity and advise doing LFTs and RFTs if deranged. Patient has severe AKI (creatinine 2.4, was 0.9) on TDF. Evidence for drug attribution: TDF is nephrotoxic. Evidence against: acute presentation with 5-day gastroenteritis, dehydration (BP 90/60, dry mucous membranes), urea:creatinine ratio 24:1 (prerenal), urinalysis without protein/glucose (no Fanconi pattern), and two family members with same illness. This clinical picture strongly favours prerenal AKI from gastroenteritis rather than TDF nephrotoxicity. Permanent discontinuation may be unnecessary if renal function recovers with fluid resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Temporarily hold TDF during acute AKI. Resuscitate with IV fluids. Recheck creatinine after rehydration before deciding on permanent TDF discontinuation.

alerts.title: TDF creatinine monitoring overdue and eGFR not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for patients on TDF. Patient's last creatinine was 2025-02-14, which is 375 days before the current visit, exceeding the 12-month interval. No eGFR was documented at either time point. The clinician's plan does not include follow-up renal function testing after resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Check serum creatinine and eGFR after IV fluid resuscitation and repeat serially to monitor renal recovery. Document eGFR with each creatinine result.
